Drafted stories cite the spec's Piton source, not its compiled Markdown. In [Spec Grounding](.claude/reference/scope/planning/index.md#spec-grounding), each entry in a proposal's `spec` list becomes a link to the element in the Piton source under the spec location. That covers both the .pi file and the element it names. Today the entry is a heading under `.claude/reference`. The short line saying what in the element the story touches stays, and so does the "No match" entry.

When a proposal arrives, the application checks each link against the Piton source: the file has to exist and has to define the named element. Any link that fails the check is dropped, with the same muted note on the card saying why. On the proposal card and in an accepted story's "Spec" list, each citation opens that place in the Piton source. Citations added by hand are picked from the spec's elements, not from the compiled reference.

The drafter still learns what the spec says only from the compiled reference or from `piton slice`, never by reading the Piton source, as [Reading The Spec](.claude/reference/scope/prompt-mode/mode-system-prompts/index.md#reading-the-spec) says. Only where its citations point changes. The story's prompt names the cited elements and links to them in the same Piton source form. The `suspense-story` format described in [Proposals](.claude/reference/scope/planning/index.md#proposals), and the planning.pi prompt among the [Baked System Prompts](.claude/reference/scope/harness-integration/baked-prompts/index.md#prompts), are updated to ask for and explain this form, with an example.

## Proposals

The agent never writes the plan itself. Its run is a Question run, as the [Sandbox](../sandbox/index.md#sandbox) says, able to read the project and change nothing, and Suspense data is never granted to it, so it can't touch `.suspense/planning/`; it only proposes, and nothing it proposes reaches the plan until the user accepts it.
Each proposal is one concrete task, with a title, a prompt, and the mode that fits it, and says where it should go: either "New story", to become a story of its own, or "Add to" a story, naming an existing story the run was shown, the open story first, to be added to it. The planning prompt of the [BakedSystemPrompts](../harness-integration/baked-prompts/index.md#baked-system-prompts) asks for each proposal as a fenced block whose info string is `suspense-story`, holding its title, its mode, its target, `new` or the story's id, its `spec` list of citations into the Piton source, as the spec grounding says, and its prompt, so the application reads it whatever else the reply says. The planning prompt explains the form with an example, as:
```suspense-story
title: Close a finished sprint
mode: chain
target: new
spec:
- spec/scope/planning/index.pi#Planning.sprint: when Close sprint shows
- No match: archiving a closed sprint
prompt:
Close sprint is offered once every story of the current sprint has
ended, as spec/scope/planning/index.pi#Planning.sprint says.
```
A block that names a story that no longer exists is shown as "New story", with a muted note saying so.

## Spec Grounding

content.text:
Almost all of this was already in the code from my earlier spec-grounding change. Proposals cite links into the Piton source, like `spec/scope/planning/index.pi#Planning.sprint`, and each is checked on arrival against the file and its declared anchor or property. A failing link is dropped with a note ("no such file" or "the file doesn't define …"). Citations open the `.pi` file at the element's declaration, "Add citation" searches the spec's elements by name, and `planning.pi` tells the drafter to read only the compiled reference or `piton slice`.

This step changed two small things:
- **Example block:** the example in the drafting and research requests is now the spec's own `#proposals` example, "Close a finished sprint", with its `spec:` list and `prompt:` key, using the project's spec location.
- **Parsing that form:** an entry like `spec/…#Planning.sprint: when Close sprint shows` used to keep the trailing colon as part of the link. It no longer does. A test now checks that the example reads back as intended.

Nothing is compiled or tested: `build.rs` calls `piton compile`, which this sandbox blocks, so I only checked syntax with rustfmt.

Two things in the spec don't line up:
- **Kind and quote:** the spec's example has neither, but Spec Grounding still asks every citation to start with Requirement, Behaviour, Name or Section and end with the quoted words. I kept both rules: the prompt's wording asks for them and the example shows the plain form.
- **Code runs:** the conflict the spec step raised is still open. A story sent as a Code task will carry links into the spec location, which a Code run's sandbox can't open. Should each element also cite its compiled reference heading, or should Code runs be allowed to read the spec source?
